WHAT WENT WRONG THE FIRST TIME, because it will happen again otherwise. Malcolm picks from CONTACT SHEETS on his Desktop named library-<product>-N.png. 'library-pdrncream-1' is a FILE, not a folder — and the batch it tiles is the v1 wave, which now lives in assets/ai-generated/_superseded/pdrn-cream-v1-PORN-label/. The first pass resolved his words against the current library FOLDER instead, which holds the v2 regeneration: a different photograph carrying the same shot id. Both are real files, both match the words 'B-face-full-prod-right gpt_image_01', and only the contact sheet disambiguates them. Pixel-compared against all three candidates, the wrongly-published image scored 0.82 mean abs difference to the v2 file and 40.30 to this one.

THE BATCH IS NAMED PORN-LABEL AND THIS FRAME IS STILL CLEAN. The fault hit 'most frames', not all. Checked at 100% and again at rendered size: Skingenetix with the dotted double-helix mark / PDRN COLLAGEN REPAIR, the D unmistakably a D / DEEP RENEWAL TREATMENT in brand red / PREMIUM FORMULA. Verify per frame, never per batch — the folder name is a warning, not a verdict.

SOURCE: 2048x848 (2.42:1), extended left to 3750x848 (4.42:1) so the full height survives to a 1920 viewport.

OBJECT-POSITION IS right center, AND THAT IS THE THIRD DIFFERENT ANSWER IN THREE BANNERS — 78% on the firming page, 93% on the previous build of this one, 100% here. It is measured, not chosen: this frame's subject runs to x=3711 of 3750, leaving only 39px of margin, so any anchor below 100% clips her hand and the jar at 1024 and 1280. At 100% the clear dark ground is still 385px at 1280, 545px at 1440 and 1025px at 1920.

CLEANER EXTENSION THAN THE FRAME IT REPLACES. Row banding measures 2.34 luminance levels peak-to-peak against a background of 18.1, against 4.15 for the v2 build. The shoulder is set at y=846 rather than None on purpose: it clips only the last two rows of the left edge, and leaving those lit rows in the profile would have drawn a bright hairline along the bottom of all 1702px of extension.
